Multiplicative Zero Replacement

Source: R/replace_zeros.r
replace_zeros_mult.Rd

Replaces every zero with a small proportion \(\delta\), and scales each sample's non-zero proportions down by the same factor so that the sample still sums to 1 (Martín-Fernández et al. 2003). The ratios between non-zero parts are unchanged.

Usage

replace_zeros_mult(counts, margin = 1L, delta = NULL)

Arguments

counts

A numeric matrix of non-negative abundances (samples \(\times\) features), or any of the objects listed under Input Types. Counts or proportions.

margin

The margin containing samples. 1 if samples are rows, 2 if samples are columns. Ignored when counts is a special object class (e.g. phyloseq). Default: 1

delta

The proportion that every zero becomes: a single value, or one value per sample (matched to the samples by name when both are named, else in order), each between 0 and 1. NULL (the default) uses \(1 / D^2\), with \(D\) the number of features, as scikit-bio does. A sample's \(\delta\) times its number of zeros must be below 1.

Value

A dense numeric matrix of proportions with no zeros, in the orientation of counts (samples \(\times\) features for margin = 1, features \(\times\) samples for margin = 2, and for a single sample given as a vector), with its names. Each sample sums to 1. Attributes:

  • method: 'mult'.

  • delta: the \(\delta\) used: one value, or one per sample (named after the samples).

  • n_replaced: the number of zeros replaced.

Details

For a sample with proportions \(x_j = c_j / \sum_k c_k\) and \(Z\) zeros, $$r_j = \delta \text{ if } x_j = 0, \qquad r_j = (1 - Z\delta)\, x_j \text{ otherwise.}$$

The \(\delta\) is the same for every sample (unless given per sample), whatever its depth: a zero in a sample of 1,000 reads and one in a sample of 100,000 become the same proportion. Choose \(\delta\) below the smallest proportion that the samples could detect, e.g. a fraction of 1 / max(depths), or give each sample its own, e.g. delta = 0.5 / rowSums(counts) (half a read).

A feature that is zero in every sample is replaced like any other zero. Samples with no non-zero values are an error: there is nothing to scale.

The result equals scikit-bio's multi_replace() (version 0.7.4) to the last bit: each sample's total is summed in numpy's (pairwise) order. Unlike scikit-bio, a \(\delta\) that would leave a sample's non-zero proportions at exactly 0 (\(Z\delta = 1\)) is an error too, so that the result has no zeros.

The result feeds straight into aitchison(), alr(), ilr() and any function with norm = 'clr', with no pseudocount.

Input Types

The counts parameter is designed to accept a simple numeric matrix, but seamlessly supports objects from the following biological data packages:

  • phyloseq

  • rbiom

  • SummarizedExperiment

  • TreeSummarizedExperiment

For large datasets, standard matrix operations may be slow. See vignette('performance') for details on using optimized formats (e.g. sparse matrices) and parallel processing.

References

Martín-Fernández, J. A., Barceló-Vidal, C., & Pawlowsky-Glahn, V. (2003). Dealing with zeros and missing values in compositional data sets using nonparametric imputation. Mathematical Geology, 35, 253–278. doi:10.1023/A:1023866030544

See also

replace_zeros(), list_zero_replacements()

Examples

    x <- replace_zeros_mult(ex_counts)
    x[1:3, 1:4]
#>        Streptococcus Bacteroides Corynebacterium Haemophilus
#> Saliva    0.44347826 0.005475040      0.02777778 0.492753623
#> Gums      0.87017181 0.004389265      0.02777778 0.095466516
#> Nose      0.02176063 0.001978239      0.49258160 0.001978239
    attr(x, 'delta')
#> [1] 0.02777778
    rowSums(x)
#> Saliva   Gums   Nose  Stool 
#>      1      1      1      1 

    # The ratios between non-zero parts are kept.
    nz <- ex_counts[1, ] > 0
    all.equal(x[1, nz] / sum(x[1, nz]), ex_counts[1, nz] / sum(ex_counts[1, nz]))
#> [1] TRUE

    # Half a read in each sample.
    x <- replace_zeros_mult(ex_counts, delta = 0.5 / rowSums(ex_counts))
    attr(x, 'delta')
#>       Saliva         Gums         Nose        Stool 
#> 0.0014492754 0.0005643341 0.0004945598 0.0008130081
